round-legal_team_member-claude-verify.grantAnalysis: Coordinator asked whether the grant (11 Toolsets + write) contradicts the person being told to choose Workspace and Read only. Server facts: the consent POST /api/v1/oauth-grants/consent came at 19:05:42Z from 100.68.96.37 (the owner's browser on this tailnet node), 30 s after the consent page loaded at 19:05:12Z. The handler stores req.body.toolsets and req.body.scope verbatim (apps/api/src/modules/oauth-grants/routes.ts) after checking each is offered; oauth_consents, the oauth_grant.granted activity payload and the access token all carry the same 11 Toolsets and write. The stored order is workspace, tasks, documents, knowledge, people, auto-docs, requests, contracts, matters, comments, entities. That is not MCP_TOOLSETS order (workspace, contracts, matters, tasks, …); it is the order the consent page's checkboxes were clicked, down column 1, up column 2 and down column 3 of the 3-column grid (consent.tsx appends each checked Toolset to its state). So the page submitted eleven individual checkbox selections and Read and write. openlaw_whoami returns the grant's Toolsets (with guide) and scope (apps/api/src/mcp/auth.ts oauthContext; register.ts), which matches Claude's answer of write and twelve Toolsets. No product defect is shown: whoami reports the grant, and the grant is what the consent page posted. Only guide Tools ran (openlaw_whoami, openlaw_docs_search, openlaw_docs_read); no Workspace or other Toolset Tool was called, although the grant made all eleven Toolsets' Tools available.

round-administrator-claude-verify.teamAndAdministration: Team and Administration were not granted: the grant, oauth_consents and the token scopes hold the other 11 Toolsets. They were not offered either: the consent page for Daniel in phase browser listed 11 checkboxes. No Tool in apps/api/src/mcp at 067c1646 declares toolset team or administration, and facts() offers a requested Toolset only when a Tool exists for it (oauth-grants/routes.ts). The ceiling still lists all 13.

round-business_user-claude-offer.offerAnalysis: The person reported: "I was surprised that it offered all of the scopes, given that this is a business user." Reproduced as Jonas Weber with a fresh request for all 13 Toolsets and write: the consent page offered 9 Toolsets (Workspace, Contracts, Matters, Requests, Comments, Documents, Auto-Docs, Entities, Knowledge) and both Read only and Read and write; Tasks, People, Team and Administration were not offered (screenshot consent-offer-business_user.png). (a) The lab has one organization Toolset ceiling for both groups, holding all 13; there is no separate Business User ceiling. (b) DD-029 register (DECISIONS.md, the Business User column) gives Business Users at least one Tool in exactly these 9 Toolsets and none in tasks, people, team and admin; DD-029 decision 4 lets the person pick within the ceiling, decision 6 says Business Users see the subset their account type permits; facts() in oauth-grants/routes.ts offers requested ∩ ceiling ∩ Toolsets with a Tool for the account type, Administration for Administrators only. The served guide says "Only the requested Toolsets your account and organization permit are offered." (c) The grant stored the same 9 and write. Result: expected behavior, not a product defect or a lab setting. Claude called it "every Toolset" because all 9 offered were chosen. Read and write is offered because Business Users have write Tools (for example Requests) and the organization is not read-only. Contrast with the support group note (Portal Request an API key dialog offers a Business User the whole ceiling including Team and Administration): the consent page does not repeat that; it filters by account type.
